govdocs-archive_org-nsia-FieldCapp_Field:
Six days after the assassination, the FBI recorded a lead about photographs. A memorandum dated November 28, 1963 states that Eddie Barker of KRLD reported that a man named Capp Field possessed photographs of the assassination. In those first days, every camera in Dealey Plaza mattered to investigators.

Amateur film and photographs became core evidence in the Kennedy case, because they fixed the shooting in frames. A report that one more man held pictures sent agents to find him. The memo preserves that lead as the Bureau logged it, part of the great gathering of images from Dallas.
nasa-tm-19690017325-cowell-type-numerica:
Jesse L. Maury Jr. and Gail P. Segal of Goddard Space Flight Center wrote this April 1969 preprint, X-553-69-46. They apply Cowell-type numerical integration to satellite orbit computation. Cowell's approach steps an orbit forward by summing every force acting on the satellite. Orbit equations have no exact written solution, so computers must build the path step by step.

The opening chapters weigh one-step methods against multistep methods for such problems. One-step methods need only the last computed point, but they err more and cost more evaluations. Multistep methods reuse several past points and reach high accuracy with larger steps. High speed computers, the authors note, made this precision practical at all. Their study puts the multistep Cowell approach to work on real satellite orbits.
